standard_prerequisites.name: In an absolutely flat ring every ideal is pure, and every finitely generated pure ideal is generated by an idempotent
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces an idempotent generating the principal ideal of any element, which drives the rest of the argument.

standard_prerequisites.name: For an idempotent of a ring the corresponding basic open subset is both open and closed, and a ring whose primes are all maximal is reduced exactly when its nilradical vanishes
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that all primes are maximal and that the ring is reduced, giving one of the conditions from absolute flatness.

standard_prerequisites.name: A reduced ring all of whose primes are maximal has all local rings fields, and a ring all of whose localizations at primes are flat has every module flat
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the last two implications of the chain, closing the cycle back to absolute flatness.

core_obligations: Record that the equivalence of the first two conditions is immediate, and start the cycle by assuming absolute flatness (proof lines 30260-30263).

Deduce that every ideal is pure and hence that every finitely generated ideal is generated by an idempotent; apply this to a principal ideal to see that the corresponding open subset is closed as well as open, and conclude that every prime is maximal and that the ring is reduced (proof lines 30263-30276).
Derive the third condition from the second: a reduced ring whose primes are all maximal has every local ring a field (proof lines 30278-30281).
Close the cycle: if every local ring is a field then every module is flat by the localization criterion, so the ring is absolutely flat again (proof lines 30283-30285).
proof_roadmap: The first equivalence is immediate; assume absolute flatness and use purity of ideals to get idempotent generators (proof lines 30260-30268).
Read off that primes are maximal and that the ring is reduced (proof lines 30268-30276).
Pass to local rings and back to flatness of all modules to close the cycle (proof lines 30278-30285).
difficulty_reason: The statement collects four descriptions of a ring of weak dimension zero: absolute flatness, reducedness with all primes maximal, and all local rings being fields (statement lines 30249-30258). The proof runs a cycle: absolute flatness makes every ideal pure, whence finitely generated ideals are generated by idempotents, which makes the basic open subsets closed and forces primes to be maximal while killing nilpotents, after which the local rings are fields and flatness of all localizations brings the argument back to absolute flatness (proof lines 30260-30285). The purity-to-idempotent step and the closedness of basic opens are the technical content of the cycle. The counted span refers six times to results of another chapter, all carried as navigation stubs.
